mainTopic: Identifying forbidden חלב, veins, sinews and membranes, and which can be fixed by salting
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that fat inside the kidneys is permitted, based on שמואל's rule that fat covered by flesh is permitted. The גמרא tests that rule against שמואל's ruling that the fat under the loins is forbidden. אביי answers, and רבי יוחנן supports him, that a living animal's joints spread apart, so that fat is not truly covered. שמואל then matches real animal fats to the Torah's phrases, and rules on the foreleg veins, which רבא explains are forbidden only because of blood, so cutting and salting fixes them. The גמרא lists the tail sinews, then five forbidden strands and five forbidden membranes, sorting each as forbidden because of חלב (no fix) or because of blood (cutting and salting works). A story about peeling a spleen leads to a ברייתא showing that the whole spleen membrane is forbidden, though only the דד brings כרת. Two ברייתות about the spleen and kidney membranes are reconciled by splitting each organ into a stricter area and a lighter area. The amud ends by opening a dispute between רב אמי and רב אסי about crushed testicles, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that fat inside the kidneys is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא uses the rule that fat covered by flesh is permitted to prove that the Torah forbids only fat on top of the kidneys, not fat inside them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fat covered by flesh is permitted. So when the Torah says 'upon the loins,' it means only the fat on top of them and not the fat inside them. In the same way, 'upon the kidneys' means the fat on top of the kidneys and not the fat inside them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof from the previous discussion. Since fat covered by flesh is permitted, fat inside the kidneys should also be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the word 'upon' (עַל) for both the loins and the kidneys. Since fat inside the loins, covered by flesh, is permitted, the word 'upon' must mean 'exposed on top.' The same word should mean the same thing for the kidneys.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of a kosher domesticated animal
Loins, the flanks near the lower back
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key rule, that fat covered by flesh is permitted. The rest of this section tests that rule.

phrases.english: Fat that the flesh covers is permitted;
apparently, the Merciful One said 'that which is upon the loins,'
and not that which is inside the loins.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי שֶׁעַל הַכְּלָיוֹת אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
phrases.english: Here too, the Merciful One said 'that which is upon the kidneys,'
and not that which is inside the kidneys.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun earlier on the daf
steps.raayaObject: Fat inside the kidneys is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's rule that fat covered by flesh is permitted, read together with the word 'upon' in the פסוק

steps.title: Restating the rule that covered fat is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to examine שמואל's rule on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: שמואל said that fat covered by flesh is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rule again because it wants to test it on its own. This sets up a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is turning from using the rule to examining the rule itself. Nothing new is added yet. This line prepares the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself, returning to examine a quoted statement

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Fat that the flesh covers is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule used in the proof and examines it directly
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fat covered by flesh is permitted

steps.title: Challenge from the forbidden fat under the loins
steps.stepSummary: Another statement of שמואל forbids the fat under the loins, even though flesh covers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that true? Didn't שמואל also say that the fat under the loins is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל seems to contradict himself. The fat under the loins is covered by flesh, yet he forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If covered fat is permitted, the fat under the loins should be permitted too. Because שמואל forbids it, either the rule is wrong or something about this fat is different.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? It opens a challenge

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abba say that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This fat that is under the loins is forbidden!
phrases.notes: The point is that flesh covers this fat, so by the first rule it should be permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just restated
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that covered fat is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself forbids the fat under the loins, which is covered by flesh

steps.title: Living animal's joints spread apart
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that when the animal is alive, its joints separate, so the fat under the loins is not really covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: when an animal is alive, its joints spread apart.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. The fat under the loins gets exposed while the animal moves, so it does not count as covered fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is whether the fat is covered while the animal is alive. The fat under the loins becomes exposed when the animal walks, so it keeps the status of exposed, forbidden fat. Both of שמואל's statements stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Separates apart, meaning the joints spread open

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule of covered fat is cancelled. It still stands. This fat simply does not count as covered, because it was exposed while the animal was alive.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
An animal in its lifetime, its joints spread apart.
phrases.notes: As it walks, the joints open and the fat underneath is exposed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּהֵמָה בְּחַיֶּיהָ פָּרוֹקֵי מִיפַּרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fat under the loins is covered, so it contradicts the rule
steps.terutzMaskana: It is exposed during the animal's life, so it is not considered covered fat

steps.title: רבי יוחנן remembers the same tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he is no butcher, but he remembers the בית מדרש saying the same thing as אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: I am not a butcher, and I am not a butcher's son, but I remember that in the study hall they used to say that an animal's joints spread apart while it is alive.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן backs up אביי's answer with a tradition he heard in the study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this is a fact about animal bodies, one might expect only a butcher to know it. רבי יוחנן admits he is not an expert, but the tradition of the בית מדרש confirms the fact.
steps.whatToRemember: The fat under the loins is forbidden even though flesh covers it after slaughter, because it was exposed while the animal was alive.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
I am not a butcher,
and I am not the son of a butcher,
phrases.notes: He means he is no expert in how an animal's body is built.

phrases.aramaic: וּנְהִירְנָא דְּהָכִי הֲווֹ אָמְרִי בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא:
phrases.english: but I remember that this is what they would say in the study hall:
An animal in its lifetime, its joints spread apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that a living animal's joints spread apart
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tradition recalled from the בית מדרש

steps.title: Fat on the stomachs is the fat 'upon the innards'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the fat on two of the stomachs is forbidden with כרת, and that it is the Torah's 'fat upon the innards'.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: the fat on the omasum and the reticulum is forbidden and punishable by כרת. This is the fat the Torah calls 'upon the innards.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement of שמואל identifies one kind of real חלב and connects it to a phrase in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says the fat is fully forbidden, not just a stricter custom, since eating it carries כרת. He also links it to the Torah's words 'the fat upon the innards.'

keyTerms.meaning: Omasum, one of the stomachs of a cud-chewing animal
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating חלב

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The fat that is on the omasum and the reticulum
is forbidden, and punishable by karet,
phrases.notes: Some versions say אסורין, in round brackets; the corrected wording is אָסוּר, in square brackets.

phrases.english: and this is the fat that is upon the innards.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: חֵלֶב שֶׁעַל הֶמְסֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New statement of שמואל on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fat on the omasum and reticulum is Torah-forbidden חלב with כרת, and it is the 'fat upon the innards'

steps.title: Tailbone fat is the fat 'upon the loins'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the fat at the tailbone area is forbidden with כרת, and that it is the Torah's 'fat upon the loins'.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: the fat at the tailbone is forbidden and punishable by כרת. This is the fat the Torah calls 'upon the loins.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another statement of שמואל in the same style identifies a second kind of real חלב with a phrase in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us what the Torah's 'fat upon the loins' actually is: the fat by the tailbone. It is forbidden with כרת, just like the fat in the step before.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל matches real animal fats to the Torah's words: the stomach fat is 'upon the innards,' and the tailbone fat is 'upon the loins.' Both carry כרת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
This fat of the tailbone is forbidden,
and punishable by karet,
and this is the fat that is upon the loins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel statement identifying another kind of חלב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tailbone fat is Torah-forbidden חלב with כרת, and it is the 'fat upon the loins'

steps.title: The veins in the foreleg are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the veins in the animal's foreleg are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב יהודה, who said in the name of שמואל: the veins in the foreleg are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל: the veins inside the foreleg of an animal may not be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling does not say why the veins are forbidden. That missing reason is exactly what the next two steps argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Strands, meaning veins or sinews inside the meat

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The veins that are in the foreleg are forbidden.
phrases.notes: "יד" here means the animal's front leg, not a human hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of שמואל's rulings about forbidden parts of the animal, now moving from fats to veins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The veins in the foreleg are forbidden.

steps.title: רב ספרא objects that the Torah never forbade meat
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא challenges: these veins are just meat, and the Torah never said not to eat meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: משה! Did the Torah say, "Do not eat meat"?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא attacks the ruling from step 8. He argues these veins are simply part of the meat, and meat is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To רב ספרא, the veins are simply part of the meat, so there seems to be no Torah reason to forbid them. Forbidding them is like forbidding meat itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, a name for ה׳, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
Moses! Did the Merciful One say
phrases.notes: Calling someone "משה" is a respectful way of saying "great scholar". He is talking to רבי אבא.

phrases.english: "Do not eat meat"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֹשֶׁה, מִי אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא לָא תֵּיכוֹל בִּישְׂרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the foreleg veins are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The veins are part of the meat, and the Torah permits meat, so there is no basis for forbidding them.

steps.title: רבא: the veins are forbidden because of blood, so cutting and salting fixes it
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the problem is the blood in the veins; if you cut and salt the leg, it is permitted even for cooking in a pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: משה! Did the Torah say, "Eat blood"? If one cuts it open and salts it, it is fine even for a pot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends שמואל's ruling by explaining its reason: the veins are full of blood. Then he gives the practical fix: cut the veins open and salt them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees the veins are not a forbidden part of the animal on their own. The problem is only the blood trapped inside them. Once cutting and salting removes that blood, the leg may be cooked in a pot, and roasting is certainly fine.

keyTerms.meaning: He salted it, to draw out the blood
A pot, meaning cooking in liquid

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the foreleg veins are forbidden only because of blood, not as a fat or a separate forbidden part. That is why a simple fix of cutting and salting works.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Moses! Did the Merciful One say
"Eat blood"?
phrases.notes: He is turning רב ספרא's words around: the veins are full of blood, and blood is forbidden.

phrases.english: If one cut it and salted it,
even for a pot it is also permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֹשֶׁה, מִי אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא אֲכוֹל דְּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ספרא's challenge by giving the reason behind שמואל's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason for the ruling, which limits it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The veins seem to be forbidden for no reason, as if they were ordinary meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The veins are forbidden because of the blood in them; after cutting and salting, the leg is permitted even for cooking in a pot.

steps.title: The fat on the first cubit of the small intestine must be scraped off
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the fat on the top אמה of the small intestine must be scraped off, and this is the 'fat on the small intestine' the חכמים spoke of.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the top אמה of the intestine needs scraping, and this is the fat on the small intestine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of שמואל, about fat on the beginning of the small intestine. He says it must be scraped off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל pinpoints exactly which fat is meant by the known phrase "חלב שעל הדקין": only the fat on the first אמה. This defines where the forbidden fat is and where scraping is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The head, or start, of the intestine
An אמה, a cubit, about half a meter
The fat on the small intestine

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The top cubit of the intestine
requires scraping,
and this is the fat that is on the small intestine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: רֵישׁ מְעַיָּא בְּאַמְּתָא בָּעֵי גְּרִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling in שמואל's list, returning from veins to forbidden fats.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fat on the first אמה of the small intestine must be scraped off; this is the חלב שעל הדקין.

steps.title: The forbidden sinews in the tail and how they branch
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that the sinews in the tail are forbidden: five of them, three on the right splitting into two each, and two on the left splitting into three each.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: the sinews in the tailbone are forbidden. There are five sinews in the tail, three on the right and two on the left. The three each split into two, and the two each split into three.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה forbids the sinews in the tail area and describes exactly how many there are and how they branch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These sinews contain forbidden fat. The detailed description (five sinews, and how each one branches) is a map for the butcher. Why that map matters is explained in the next step.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
The sinews that are in the tailbone are forbidden.
There are five sinews in the tail,
three on the right and two on the left.
The three each split into two,
the two each split into three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: חוּטִין שֶׁבָּעוֹקֶץ אֲסוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about another forbidden part, the tail sinews.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five sinews in the tail are forbidden; the three on the right split into two each, and the two on the left split into three each.

steps.title: Why the detailed count matters: removing the sinews while warm
steps.stepSummary: The detail matters because while the meat is still warm the sinews pull out easily; if it has cooled, one must dig after each of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference: if he pulls them out while they are still warm, they come out; if not, he has to dig after them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב יהודה described the sinews in such detail. It answers an unspoken question: why does the count matter?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after שחיטה, while the meat is warm, the sinews slide out easily. Once the meat cools, the butcher must dig into the flesh after each branch, so he needs to know how many there are to be sure he got them all.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical difference that comes out of this

phrases.english: The practical difference is,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי שָׁלֵיף לְהוּ עַד דְּחַמִּימֵי – מִשְׁתַּלְּפִי,
phrases.english: that if he pulls them out while they are still warm, they are pulled out,
and if not, he needs to dig after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the purpose of the detailed description in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Unspoken question: why does it matter how many sinews there are and how they branch?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When warm, the sinews pull out easily; when cold, one must dig after each one, so the count is needed to remove them all.

steps.title: Five forbidden strands: three for fat, two for blood
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב יהודה) sums up: five strands are forbidden. Those of the spleen, tail and kidneys are forbidden because of חלב; those of the foreleg and throat are forbidden because of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say רב יהודה: there are five strands; three because of fat and two because of blood. Those of the spleen, tail and kidneys are because of fat; those of the foreleg and throat are because of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a summary list of five forbidden strands and gives the reason for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list splits the strands into two groups by reason. The spleen, tail and kidney strands hold forbidden fat, so they must be removed. The foreleg and throat veins hold blood. This fits רבא's point in step 10 that the foreleg veins are only a blood problem.
steps.whatToRemember: Five strands are forbidden. Spleen, tail and kidneys are forbidden because of fat, and must be removed. Foreleg and throat are forbidden because of blood, which is why cutting and salting is enough for them.

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say Rav Yehuda:
There are five strands,
three because of forbidden fat,
and two because of blood.
Those of the spleen, of the tail and of the kidneys are because of fat,
those of the foreleg and of the throat are because of blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יְהוּדָה: חַמְשָׁא חוּטֵי הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the forbidden strands discussed so far, including the foreleg veins and tail sinews, and gives the reason for each.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five strands are forbidden: those of the spleen, tail and kidneys because of fat, and those of the foreleg and throat because of blood.

steps.title: Why does it matter if a strand is forbidden for fat or for blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the strands forbidden because of חלב and those forbidden because of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the list from step 14: why does it matter which reason forbids each strand? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 sorted the five strands into two groups, חלב and blood. Both groups are forbidden, so the גמרא wants to know what we gain from knowing the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: What difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical point of the two-way sorting in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between strands forbidden because of חלב and those forbidden because of blood.

steps.title: Blood strands can be fixed; fat strands cannot
steps.stepSummary: Strands forbidden because of blood become permitted if you cut and salt them. Strands forbidden because of חלב can never be fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ones forbidden because of blood: if you cut them open and salt them, they are fine. The others have no fix.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: blood can be removed, so cutting and salting those strands makes them permitted. חלב is forbidden in itself, so those strands must be taken out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is a problem only because it is inside the meat, and salting draws it out. חלב is a forbidden substance in its own right, and no method can make it permitted. This matches רבא's answer in step 10 about cutting and salting the leg.

keyTerms.meaning: A fix; a way to make it permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Blood strands: cut and salt, then permitted. חלב strands: must be removed, with no fix.

phrases.english: These, which are forbidden because of blood,
if one cuts them open and salts them,
they are fine (permitted).
Those (the fat ones) have no fix.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blood strands can be made permitted by cutting and salting. חלב strands can never be made permitted.

steps.title: Five forbidden membranes: three for fat, two for blood
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא (or רב יהודה) says five membranes are forbidden. The spleen, tail and kidney membranes are forbidden because of חלב. The testicle and brain membranes are forbidden because of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are five forbidden membranes, three because of fat and two because of blood. The membranes of the spleen, the tail and the kidneys are forbidden because of fat. The membranes of the testicles and the brain are forbidden because of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: A new list is given, this time of membranes (thin skins) rather than strands. Each one is sorted as forbidden either because of חלב or because of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list is set up just like the strands list in step 14, but it is about membranes. Because of step 16, the sorting tells us which ones can be fixed by cutting and salting (testicles, brain) and which must be removed completely (spleen, tail, kidneys).

keyTerms.meaning: Membranes; thin skins covering an organ

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 14. Step 14 listed five strands (חוטין). This step lists five membranes (קרמי). The two lists are similar but not the same.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said, and some say it was Rav Yehuda:
There are five forbidden membranes:
three because of forbidden fat,
and two because of blood.
Those of the spleen, of the tail, and of the kidneys
are forbidden because of fat;
those of the testicles and of the brain, because of blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel list to step 14, applied to membranes instead of strands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five membranes are forbidden. Spleen, tail and kidney membranes are forbidden because of חלב. Testicle and brain membranes are forbidden because of blood.

steps.title: Story: לוי tells the spleen-peeler to dig deeper
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר אושעיא was peeling the membrane off a spleen for לוי, only from the top. לוי told him to dig in more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר אושעיא was peeling a spleen for לוי, son of רב הונא בר חייא. He was cutting it only from the upper part. לוי said to him: Dig into it more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about the spleen membrane from step 17. It sets up a disagreement about how much of the membrane must be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The peeler removed only the membrane on the top of the spleen. לוי was stricter and wanted the membrane further down removed too. The next step shows his father's reaction.

keyTerms.meaning: Dig into it more; go further down

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Oshaya
was peeling a spleen

phrases.aramaic: לְלֵוִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא,
phrases.english: for Levi, the son of Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya.
He was cutting it only from the upper part.
Levi said to him: Go down into it more.
phrases.notes: לוי wants the membrane removed from the lower parts of the spleen as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא הֲוָה קָא קָלֵיף לֵיהּ טְחָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical story about the spleen membrane listed in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי treats the spleen membrane as needing removal beyond the upper surface.

steps.title: The father: the תורה forbids only the membrane on the thick top part
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא quotes רב ירמיה בר אבא in the name of רב: the תורה forbids only the membrane on the דד, the thick upper part of the spleen.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father came and found him. He said: Your mother's father said this in the name of רב, and who is that? רב ירמיה בר אבא. The תורה forbade only the membrane on the thick top part.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי's father arrives and tells him he is being too strict. He quotes רב that the תורה only forbids the membrane on the thick top of the spleen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the prohibition from step 17: it is not the membrane of the whole spleen, only the part on the דד. That supports the peeler, who cut only from the top, against לוי's demand to dig deeper.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה did not forbid (anything but this)
Literally "breast"; here, the thick, bulging upper part of the spleen

phrases.english: His father came and found him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר אֲבוּהּ דְּאִמָּךְ מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what your mother's father said in the name of Rav,
and who is he? Rav Yirmeya bar Abba:
phrases.notes: The "who" is the grandfather, not רב. The grandfather was רב ירמיה בר אבא.

phrases.english: The Torah forbade nothing
except the membrane on the thick top part alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to לוי's strict instruction in step 18 with a ruling that limits the prohibition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה prohibition of the spleen membrane applies only to the membrane on the דד.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids the membrane on the whole spleen
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רב המנונא says the spleen membrane is forbidden but carries no כרת. That cannot mean the דד membrane, which the תורה forbids, so it must mean the membrane on the whole spleen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't רב המנונא say that a ברייתא teaches: the membrane on the spleen is forbidden, but one is not liable for it? What case is this? If it means the membrane on the thick top part, why is one not liable? So it must mean the membrane of the whole spleen.
steps.whatsHappening: The father's ruling is challenged with a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows that the rest of the spleen's membrane is also forbidden, which backs up לוי's demand to dig deeper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father said the תורה forbids the דד membrane, so eating it should carry real punishment (כרת). The ברייתא speaks of a membrane that is forbidden but carries no punishment, so it cannot be the דד. It must be the membrane on the rest of the spleen, which is forbidden on a lower level. So the lower part cannot simply be left on.

keyTerms.meaning: One is not punishable for it (no כרת)
What is the case? How do we picture it?

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not argue that the דד is permitted. Its point is that the other parts are also forbidden, just without the תורה-level punishment.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rav Hamnuna say:
It was taught: the membrane on the spleen is forbidden,
but one is not liable for it.
phrases.notes: "Not liable" means no כרת for eating it, even though it is forbidden.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say it is the membrane on the thick top part,
why is one not liable for it?
Rather, it means the membrane of the whole spleen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the father's ruling in step 19 that only the דד membrane matters.
steps.kashyaTarget: The father's claim that only the membrane on the דד is forbidden, which implies the rest may be left on.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes a spleen membrane that is forbidden without punishment. That cannot be the תורה-forbidden דד, so it must be the rest of the spleen, which is therefore also forbidden.

steps.title: The father accepts the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא answers: if it is taught in a ברייתא, then it is taught. He accepts that the membrane on the whole spleen is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The father does not argue back. He accepts the ברייתא, so the membrane on the whole spleen must be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His ruling still holds on the level of תורה law: only the דד membrane carries the תורה prohibition. But because of the ברייתא, the rest of the membrane is also forbidden, without punishment. In practice, לוי was right to have it peeled deeper.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is taught, it is taught; I accept the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The spleen membrane on the דד is forbidden by the תורה. The membrane on the rest of the spleen is also forbidden, but without כרת, so the whole membrane should be peeled off.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for preparing a spleen: peeling only the top is not enough.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.
phrases.notes: He means: a ברייתא is a strong source, so I accept it and won't argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge from step 20 without offering a rebuttal.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא stands: the membrane on the whole spleen is forbidden. Only the דד membrane carries the תורה prohibition with punishment.

steps.title: Back to the teaching of רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא of רב המנונא: the membranes on the spleen and on the kidney are forbidden, but eating them does not bring כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רב המנונא said that a ברייתא teaches: the membrane on the spleen is forbidden, but one does not get כרת for it. The membrane on the kidney is forbidden, but one does not get כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'גופא' to show it is going back to look closely at a teaching it quoted earlier. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 only the spleen half of this ברייתא was used, to challenge רב. Here the גמרא quotes the whole thing, including a second rule about the kidney membrane. Both rules say the same thing: the membrane is forbidden, but eating it does not bring כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא is going back to study a source it mentioned earlier
A membrane, a thin skin covering an organ
Forbidden, but there is no כרת punishment for eating it

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rav Hamnuna said: it was taught in a baraita,
the membrane that is on the spleen is forbidden
but one is not liable for it,
the membrane that is on the kidney is forbidden
but one is not liable for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא quoted in step 20 to study it in full
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The membranes on the spleen and the kidney are forbidden, but eating them does not bring כרת.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says there is liability
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that says one IS liable to כרת for these membranes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another ברייתא teaches that one is liable to כרת for them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different ברייתא says the opposite: eating these membranes does bring כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two ברייתות seem to disagree about the very same membranes. One says there is no כרת, and the other says there is. The גמרא now has to show how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for it, here meaning liable to כרת

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita: one is liable for it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a second ברייתא against the ברייתא of רב המנונא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of רב המנונא, which says there is no liability for the spleen and kidney membranes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא rules that there is liability for the same membranes, so the two sources contradict each other.

steps.title: Spleen: the דד versus the rest of the spleen
steps.stepSummary: The two rulings about the spleen do not clash. The one that gives liability means the membrane on the דד, and the one that does not means the membrane elsewhere on the spleen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Spleen against spleen is no problem. This ברייתא is talking about the membrane on the דד, and that one is talking about the membrane that is not on the דד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the spleen half of the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different part of the spleen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that gives liability means the membrane on the דד, the thick upper part, which the תורה forbids. The ברייתא that gives no liability means the membrane on the rest of the spleen, which is forbidden but carries no כרת. This fits what רב taught in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult': the contradiction can be solved
'This one... that one...': each source is talking about a different case
On the דד, the thick upper part of the spleen
'Spleen against spleen': the clash between the two rulings about the spleen

phrases.english: Spleen against spleen is not difficult:
this one is on the thick part,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that gives liability. It matches רב's rule in step 19 that the תורה forbids the דד membrane.

phrases.english: that one is not on the thick part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the spleen half of the contradiction from step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is talking about a different area of the organ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be talking about the same spleen membrane.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is liability for the membrane on the דד. For the rest of the spleen, the membrane is forbidden but carries no כרת.

steps.title: Kidney: the upper part versus the lower part
steps.stepSummary: The two rulings about the kidney do not clash either. The one that gives liability means the upper part of the kidney, and the one that does not means the lower part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Kidney against kidney is also no problem. This ברייתא is talking about the upper part, and that one is talking about the lower part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the kidney half of the contradiction the same way, by splitting the kidney into an upper part and a lower part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The membrane on the upper part of the kidney carries כרת. The membrane on the lower part is forbidden but carries no כרת. So both ברייתות are correct, each about a different area.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper one, here the upper part of the kidney
The lower one, here the lower part of the kidney

steps.whatToRemember: Each membrane has a stricter area that brings כרת (the spleen's דד, the kidney's upper part) and a lighter area that is forbidden but brings no כרת (the rest of the spleen, the kidney's lower part).

phrases.english: Kidney against kidney is also not difficult:
this one is on the upper part,
that one is on the lower part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same kind of answer as step 24, this time for the kidney
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: upper area versus lower area
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be talking about the same kidney membrane.
steps.terutzMaskana: The membrane on the upper part of the kidney brings כרת. The membrane on the lower part is forbidden only.

steps.title: רב אמי and רב אסי argue about crushed testicles
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: about testicles that were crushed, one of רב אמי and רב אסי forbids eating them and the other permits it. The גמרא starts to explain the one who forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: About crushed testicles, רב אמי and רב אסי disagree: one forbids them and one permits them. The one who forbids holds that...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a dispute about crushed testicles. It then starts to explain the reason of the one who forbids, and that explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These testicles were crushed while the animal was still alive. The question is whether they may be eaten after the animal is slaughtered. We are only told that one sage forbids and one permits, without saying which is which, and the words 'מאן דאסר' introduce the reasoning that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The one who forbids': introduces that opinion's reasoning

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say whether רב אמי or רב אסי is the one who forbids. 'חד... וחד' only tells us that they disagree.

phrases.english: Crushed testicles,
Rav Ami and Rav Asi:
one forbids and one permits.
The one who forbids holds that…

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּיעֵי חֲשִׁילָתָא, רַב אַמֵּי וְרַב אַסִּי – חַד אָסַר וְחַד שָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the membrane discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute about crushed testicles: one sage forbids eating them and one permits it.
